smell_validity.evidence: Verbatim used-row, cursor-row and percent measurements are pasted into three layers — terminal painter, Lua glue, text-object engine — while View owns the layout data; view.c's own percent computation was deleted and it now consumes composed strings from the UI backend. Misplaced ownership, repeat-edit cost, and the healthy boundary (View measures, consumers present) are unmistakable without any label.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Any change to screen-row or progress semantics must be replicated across four files and layers with no structural marker linking them; the prompt itself reports edits repeated and duplicated logic orphaned. Removing it restores a lasting View ownership boundary rather than easing one local edit, fitting a long-term trap.

development_plausibility.evidence: Four user-motivated features land in each module's idiom: a ui_window_* helper beside its siblings, an LDoc-documented Lua method registered like window.status, an enum-indexed text-object entry, a scrollbar painted through existing ui_draw_string/cell machinery. Copy-at-point-of-use walks are exactly the shortcut pragmatic patches take with a public embedded View; no scaffolding or filler is visible.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Names all four features, their semantics and the six Lua fields exactly matching the code; forbids feature redesign and shapeless wrappers; enumerates the preservation boundary (Top's cursor-row condition, 1–100 percent, empty range outside the viewport, tests and API) plus concrete verification. This decisively prevents wrong direction, incomplete cleanup and irrelevant redesign while leaving the owner API shape open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Four purposes need distinct code-supported decisions: status classification (All/Top/Bot, cursor row 0, 1–100 percent), scrollbar geometry (MIN(height,used) track, rounded thumb, notch row), Lua marshalling pinned to six documented integer values, and text-object byte ranges with wrapped-row coalescing bounded by the viewport. Each decision is anchored in different code.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt lists all four features; implementations surface via named searches (scrollinfo, scrollbar, the indicator call in view.c's status update, the SCREENLINE table entry) plus header and method-table inspection for what to retire. Each consumer's inclusion is evident from its own walk; no cross-component behavior must be combined.

repair_coordination.evidence: Owner-provided facts must preserve one shared semantics across surfaces: the status segment, scrollbar geometry and documented Lua field values. If only some sites migrate, or derivation semantics change in one place, the status bar and win:scrollinfo disagree for the same window state while ordinary tests still pass. A shared rule spans locations without a deeper interlock.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Three sites share verbatim used-row, cursor-row and percent derivations; extracting them once into view-layer accessors repairs the indicator, scrollbar and scrollinfo (about 75 percent) with identical semantics. The text object's byte-range walk needs a second, purpose-specific owner API with wrap coalescing and viewport bounds, so one uniform rule stays below 80 percent.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Dropping the wrap extension, the viewport bounds check, or the MIN(height,used) clamp compiles and passes ordinary files; failure needs wrapped long lines, off-viewport positions, or files shorter than the window. The injection ships no tests and the prompt demands manual render checks, so at least two distinct hidden paths go unchecked.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
